challenge.hidden_assumption: That every call in tls.py should be windowless. Some may be interactive by design or Linux-only; the build judges each call and the proof reads the marker for an intended window.

Measured 2026-11-20: 1 file(s) in cairn/tools/bus_client call subprocess with neither helper keyword set.
challenge.real_collision: None found: it applies the helper's existing contract and edits only files this component owns. Law 9: the red the widened scan names is the measure.

answers.falsifier: Done when unhelped_sites over cairn/tools/bus_client names nothing and the component's own proofs read as before. Wrong if a named call is interactive by design and the helper cannot express that.
answers.from_idea: none, because the sweep is cast from the widened scan's measured gap, cairn/tools/windowless_spawn/windowless_spawn.py, under ticket 364704f371dd
answers.how: Edit each named file so its subprocess.run/call/check_call/check_output/Popen calls take windowless_kwargs() (attached) or detached_kwargs() (detached), judged call by call; a call that must show a terminal on purpose says so in a comment the proof can read. A red-first proof asserts unhelped_sites over cairn/tools/bus_client names nothing.
answers.traces_to: CP4 (the system serves the person at the box: no popups while he works) and Law 4 (enforced by the widened scan, not by memory). Rule 1: the build lives inside its own component.
answers.what: Every subprocess spawn in cairn/tools/bus_client (tls.py) takes its keywords from cairn.tools.windowless_spawn, so none opens a visible console window on Windows.
